"A lot of the sounds in the game are quite unique."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"We bought a wonderful sample library from a piano in Chernobyl that someone had found in the Forbidden Zone. Someone went there and made a sample library from that old piano. So we bought that one and used it," via Arc Raiders' YouTube channel.

Arc Raiders has a terrific soundscape, although it can sometimes be hard to hear it when you're getting hunted down by your fellow players or bloodthirsty arcs. The game is quite quiet, aside from the occasional sound of distant gunfire, the clicks and cracks from small roaming arcs, and the noise of shuffling scrap as raiders sort through abandoned buildings for valuable items. But perhaps the best noise in all of Arc Raiders comes from the few instruments raiders can find amid the rubble.

"One of the gameplay designers, really early on, made a trumpet," Pajor says. "And it was so out of place, and we were like 'why are we making it?'" The musical items in Arc Raiders serve multiple purposes. There's the social incentive to play an instrument, to bond with strangers and just show them that you're a harmless, relatively chill dude. But there's also the strategic purpose of using noises to lure arcs. Perhaps you're herding them into a trap or ambush or maybe you're trying to distract the aggro of one arc away from another vulnerable player.

Avid players of Arc Raiders will notice, however, that there's no trumpet available in game. Well that's because the trumpet eventually became what we now know as the lure grenade. Apparently a playable trumpet was just too silly to the devs at first, so they settled on something a bit more useful. But now, over a year later from launch players can enjoy multiple instruments like the piano, guitar, harmonica, flute, banjo, recorder, and the trusty shaker.

"It's been almost seven years of exploring this world. [Composers Patrik Andrén and Johan Söderqvist] used to be performing musicians before they became composers so they have a lot of friends who are Sweden's best jazz musicians," Pajor adds. "So a lot of the sounds in the game are quite unique because they are making the sound libraries.

"It's their commitment to building a world; they're phenomenal world builders. So eager to understand what the game is and what the world is. They are also very demanding to work with, because they have so many ideas."

Aside from the Chernobyl piano, which is certainly one of the stranger sources of music I've heard of, composers Andrén and Söderqvist are also known for their abstract use of everyday items to make music and noises.

A lot of raw synthesisers are used to create arc-adjacent noises, but they've also hooked up different kinds of fruits to a synthesiser to grab some slightly weirder sounds. All in all, out of a three hour recording session there's usually only three minutes of usable sounds, "because it's sheer weirdness" but those three minutes "are really really really cool", Söderqvist adds, and stresses that you simply can't obtain these fantastically strange sounds another way.

#3799. Forza director, who'd been with Turn 10 for 27 years leaves Microsoft, following studios merger with Playground Games

Dan Greenawalt, director, founder, and vice president at Turn 10 Games, has departed from the studio after spending 27 years as part of the company. This comes as Turn 10 is merged with Playground Games as part of Xbox's mass restructuring initiative that made headlines as it resulted in 3200 layoffs and four studio closures earlier this year.

In a report by The Verge, an internal memo written by Playground Games studio head Trevor Williams states: "Dan Greenawalt has decided that this is the right time for him to retire from Microsoft".

The memo continues: "It's hard to overstate Dan's impact over the past 27 years. From shipping Project Gotham Racing on the original Xbox in 2001 to leading the creation of Forza, founding Turn 10 Studios and appearing so many times on our E3 stage, usually making a dramatic entrance with a supercar in tow – and so much more – we owe tremendous thanks and gratitude to Dan. On behalf of both teams, I would like to thank Dan for his leadership, his support, and his partnership. I wish him well for whatever comes next.".

With Xbox's merger of Playground Games and Turn 10, the developers will be working in collaboration on the Forza and Fable franchises. The final track racer game that Playground Games developed prior to this merger was 2023's Forza Motorsport reboot, a wonderful racer that offered a sweet alternative to the more arcade Forza Horizon series. In Eurogamer's review, the game was described as: "A generous and lavish racer, with thrilling driving, that wants you for the long haul.".

Grasshopper Manufacture, now independent of Netease Games as of the beginning of October, has been seeking to define what its trajectory will be without the benefit of that financial backing. Suda51, the studio’s founder, sat down with a number of Japanese outlets to discuss the future of the company, how plans have changed since it went independent, and the future of its No More Heroes series.

According to Suda51, one of the biggest shifts that will occur as a result of this independence and lack of financial backing is in the scale of the games the studio will be capable of developing. Under NetEase, the company had promised to develop three large games within 10 years, with February’s Romeo Is a Dead Man being one of these.Â These plans will have to be adapted, he explains in an interview with 4Gamer. âThat was a plan we made based on a promise given to NetEase at the time, so that will have to change,â he said, adding, âAs an independent studio itâs now possible to take on various jobs. I want to not just work on my own titles, but also on various interesting IPs.â Speaking to Famitsu in a separate interview, he even mentions two series heâd love to work with: Mobile Suit Gundam and Marvelâs Deadpool.

Suda51 admits that itâs a difficult time to become independent. The company handled promotion and the release of Romeo Is a Dead Man in-house, even though it had initially been planned as a NetEase work. Speaking to 4Gamer, he says promoting the title was a challenge for the studio because of how the industry has evolved in recent years. âRaising awareness for a game is really difficult,â he admits. âThatâs because compared to the old promotion, PR and marketing cycle, this era is completely different. Before, it was a challenge over how many TV commercials you could do, how much you were advertising in magazines or online. But thatâs not the case anymore.â To counter the challenges of advertising in the modern era, the studio hopes to take advantage of the Grasshopper brand to some extent. âWeâve been a studio for around 30 years, and our name has even become recognizable overseas to a point, and Iâve realized that there has to be a way we can use that and make more use of our brand power.â

As it looks to the future, the company is examining platforms, including Roblox, as a way to allow it toÂ  experiment with ideas, and it’s actively recruiting new members to the team. Earlier this year, to mark the release of Romeo Is a Dead Man, the company held a demo event in Shibuya PARCO, a department store in Tokyo, where it proudly announced that another new game would be releasing this year. While that hasnât come to fruition, Suda51 is insisting this unknown game will be released next year.

In his conversation with Famitsu, he was more specific about what he wanted to create next. âI have a few ideas of what to make next, but one thing Iâm thinking about is a game I made while I was still at Human, called Moonlight Syndrome. That was the game that started my career, and from there I made The Silver Case, Flower, Sun and Rain and Killer7. I really want to channel that idea once again if I can. I think No More Heroes has given many people the impression of Grasshopper as a bright and flashy action game studio, but I want to return to the side of the studio that specializes in the dark, serious, and chaotic ideas that we worked on until Killer7.â

Notably, Moonlight Syndrome, released by Human Entertainment in 1997 for PlayStation, has yet to be officially released overseas. At the very least Suda hopes to make this work an international release at last. And perhaps a return to No More Heroes is also in the cards. Speaking about Marvelous, which owns the No More Heroes IP, he said the company is “very aware [that next year is the 20th anniversary of No More Heroes], so Iâd love for us to do something to mark the occasion. Iâm hoping to do something special, so please look forward to it. Travis Touchdown is definitely coming back!â

Based on these interviews, it seems that the now-independent Grasshopper Manufacture is a studio that wishes to look back, as well as look to the future. While its plans have changed since it first signed with NetEase, it wants to at least stick to the intent it previously had, if not at quite the same scale, while creating things that fans of the studio will enjoy.

Becca Devens decided to celebrate Halloween by dressing up the pool float he used the most in the house. #3796. EA reportedly closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between Mass Effect 5 and Star Wars Battlefront 3

And it chose the "less risky, more predictable bet".

A new report has revealed that EA closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between investing in one of two sci-fi projects: a new Mass Effect game or a new Star Wars Battlefront game. And it chose the latter.

The revelation comes from Bloomberg, which heard from "people familiar with the company's strategy" that the "recent emergence" of an opportunity to develop a third Battlefront game meant EA - a company saddled with $18bn in debt because of the recent leveraged buyout - would have two sci-fi projects, each likely to cost hundreds of millions of dollars to make.

It couldn't afford to make both of them so EA executives chose Star Wars Battlefront 3, because it was seen "as a less risky, more predictable bet than a new Mass Effect", Bloomberg reported - despite development for the game not even having begun yet.

An EA spokesperson said the company had "collectively reached this decision following months of planning, review, and analysis, including careful consideration of evolving business conditions, industry dynamics, and our long-term priorities". "While this is never easy," the spokesperson went on, "we ultimately have to make tough decisions to focus our teams on the biggest opportunities for our future, including investing in new projects across our portfolio."

The report highlights a few other contributing factors in EA's decision, including BioWare's unfavourable recent track record and a reorganisation of its executive ranks to include more EA Sports people, in favour of those advocating for BioWare. EA bosses even lamented Dragon Age: Veilguard's sales, suggesting it would have been better if the title was 'a live service game'.

Last week, following the announcement of BioWare's closure and the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, an internal video for the project - known as Mass Effect Universe - was leaked, showing what appears to be a pre-rendered visualisation of it. The game was said to take place 600 years after the Reaper war, in the midst of a galactic cold war, and to have the player be "a cross between John Wick and James Bond" in terms of what they'd be capable of.

There was a promise of "Hitman-style freedom" in approaching levels, romance that "wasn't being sanitised", and for connections between the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies. It's not clear how much work was done on it, but clearly a lot of planning had been done - far more, certainly, than has been done on Battlefront 3.

EA's Star Wars Battlefront 2 was released in 2017 and struggled, initially, to convince - partly because it was riddled with loot boxes. But years of adjustments and improvements left it in a much better place.

#3795. Best Roblox song IDs

There’s just something about listening to your favorite music in a public setting and forcing it upon the ears of others. Roblox has turned this real-world nuisance into a series of games on its platform.

Using a database of uploaded songs, players can input Song IDs to blast their song of choice directly into the ears of strangers all over the world. Here are some of the best.

Prior to a change in March 2022, users could upload virtually any audio file and have it be playable in any game that supported the boombox via a Song ID. The change retroactively made any audio longer than six seconds private. This meant that if you weren’t the person who had originally uploaded the audio file, you would no longer be able to play or hear the sound.

This means the vast majority of Song ID repositories are now functionally useless, and users have been restricted to a much smaller selection of songs and sound clips of varying quality. One important thing to know is that there’s no guarantee that any individual Song ID may work, as they can be made private by either Roblox staff or the user who uploaded it.

Below are 30 absolute bangers to entertain yourself and possibly others around you. I have personally confirmed that each is working at the time of this writing. Go forth, aspiring DJs!

To search for music codes on Roblox, follow these steps:

You’ll discover many sections on the Audio page, from the top Roblox Song IDs to the newest hits of the day. After you find a song, you can get its ID through ‘More Info.’ Discover the correct number from your URL. For instance, mine came out to ‘create.roblox.com/store/asset/75793628822368/Mirage-Portal.’ Thus, the bolded numbers would be utilized as the Song ID.

Playing music in Roblox varies in each game, as they all have different methods. Sometimes, it can cost money with Robux, while other times, it doesn’t cost a thing. To play music for free, play Catalog Heaven, a game that allows you to customize your avatar and battle nearby bases. Once you start playing, select ‘Catalog’ and type in Boombox. There will be a few choices here, including the Boombox Gear 3.0 and Golden Super Fly Boombox. Choose one of them to trigger a prompt to enter Roblox music codes.

Tap on the Boombox again if you want to change songs. You can also stop the music by unequipping it in your inventory. Besides Catalog Heaven, you can see if other games permit music. I discovered that Jailbreak features a Car Stereo mechanic, costing 200 Robux. With this title, you can type in ‘R’ or tap the radio on the bottom-right corner of the screen. Then, enter any Song ID you prefer to listen to some tunes on Jailbreak.

For the most part, it seems like Roblox titles that use music codes require a subscription pass. Therefore, if you’re unsure whether your game is compatible, check the title’s Subscription & Passes section to see if there’s a radio or stereo feature.

Only Roblox game developers can create custom music playlists. It’s associated with a tool used in scripting to create soundtracks for various worlds. If you’re a player, you must manually enter each ID to make your own version of a playlist.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While I go 'oo' at every perfectly lit videogame vista, ray tracing can sometimes make my gaming rig go 'HNNNG'. I love a traced ray as much as the next person, but realistic reflections and lighting can be a bit of a memory hog. Thankfully, Microsoft is previewing something new for DirectX that could significantly take the load off many ageing rigs.

It's a pair of features called 'Clustered Geometry' and 'Partitioned TLAS'. At the risk of oversimplifying, you can think of this DirectX update as bringing tech very similar to Nvidia RTX Mega Geometry to every other GPU vendor.

Obviously there's more to it than that, though, with Microsoft describing this as the "most significant update [to DXR] since its debut in 2018." Top line: Microsoft's own testing of this update suggests it could reduce ray tracing memory load by as much as 90% without the need for a team green GPU (via Techspot).

So, how does it work? Well, without this update, ray tracing is already beaming between less detailed versions of the geometry you see in-game. Traditional ray tracing tech does this because bouncing around detailed models afresh for every frame would simply take too long.

Clustered geometry slices up the detailed models into neat little packages of 256 triangles or fewer. Partitioned TLAS then does a similar thing for the entire videogame vista, splitting a scene into smaller regions. Why? Well, rather than searching the entire map every time, looking for what's changed and updating the frame accordingly, the ol' dread pirate Ray Tracing needs only to run their finger over the quadrants they know are different, marking the spot with 'X'—or something like that, the metaphor got away from me a bit in the middle there.

Basically, this fresh DirectX tech massively simplifies the ray tracing data your rig has to check and update frame to frame. That could free up a whole lotta memory, with Microsoft demonstrating a reduction of 7.5 GB to 774 MB on an AMD Radeon RX 9070. Obviously, frame rates also benefitted, jumping from a wince-worthy 1.2 fps to a very impressive 79 fps in Microsoft's testing.

Now, this isn't really a case of simply installing an update and, 'whee, you're flying!' Microsoft issues a fair few caveats—for one thing, not all games are going to replicate the wins its specialised test environment saw.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

For another, working with clustered geometry and all of those packages of up to 256 triangles uses a lot more temporary scratch memory compared to traditional tech—that presents its own logistical concerns for game developers.

It's also worth reiterating that this update is not yet widely available, and there's no word yet on when PC gamers like you and me will be able to get our mitts on it either. If you feel like going sicko mode, though, Microsoft writes you can gain access to experimental features like this by using "matching Agility SDK preview headers and runtime, a supporting driver, and Windows Developer Mode."

Still, the potential to cut down memory usage without needing to buy any new hardware is very promising during these times of runaway pricing for both memory and GPUs. If I can put off a pricey upgrade for a few years more, I'll be happy.

It’s the one and only Seagal movie that is truly worth appointment viewing, and that’s for quite a few reasons, like the bonkers cast, the really cool shooting location, and, of course, Seagal at his physical peak (he’s a long way from that today). It should be, in my opinion, considered one of the best action movies of the 1990s.

You really have to kick this conversation off with the incredible cast of Under Siege. It’s rare that there are any other stars in a Seagal movie other than Seagal himself. That’s not true here. Instead of a faceless villain, we get Tommy Lee Jones as William Strannix, a former CIA operative with a serious case of narcissism. Jones is amazing in the role, as he so often is as a bad guy. The scene with Strannix eating roast beef with a chef's knife is peak ‘90s cinema. Usually, Seagal’s foes are two-dimensional, but not here.

Playing Strannix's sidekick is none other than Gary Busey. Sure, Busey doesn’t exactly have the best reputation in 2026, but in 1992, he was still thought of as a great actor, and he’s great here. He’s weaselly and slimy, and so easy to hate. He’s more hateable than Jones, that’s for sure. He’s actually perfect for the role at this point in his career. He’s a little crazy, but not too crazy, and it pays off on screen.

One of the movie's coolest aspects is its setting. At its heart, Under Siege is a heist movie, and Strannix and his band of thieves are targeting missiles on the USS Missouri, intended for the black market, hoping to spark World War III. In that respect, Strannix is basically a Bond villain trying to pull off an audacious crime to set in motion huge global changes. While shooting on the actual USS Missouri, one of the most decorated battleships in US Naval history, would have been tough to set up, they did shoot much of the movie on the USS Alabama, a retired World War II ship.

The Alabama and the Missouri are different class battleships, but they were both built just before or during the war, and are pretty similar. In a normal Seagal movie, you’d expect the whole thing to be filmed on a soundstage in Burbank, but not this one. They used a real ship, and it makes all the difference in how the movie looks. You really feel like you’re on the Missouri in this, and you believe that Seagal’s character, Casey Ryback, is a former Navy SEAL.

Seagal is really at the peak of his powers in Under Siege. He was coming off a wildly successful string of lower-budget action movies in the late ‘80s and early ‘90s, and he was ready for a big-time movie. In a lot of his later films (including Under Siege 2), he’s simply not believable as an unstoppable force, but he is in Under Siege, for sure. Though he’s been out of the spotlight for a long time, I do love going back to those early movies and remembering why Seagal was great and considered one of the biggest action stars of the ‘90s. Under Siege is the number one reason for that.

#3791. Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3's online servers are temporarily going dark, FromSoftware announces

Things might get even darker over in the world of Lordran without those silly, only sometimes helpful notes left by other players. Developer FromSoftware has announced that it's temporarily closing Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 servers because of an unspecified issue.

"Due to a server issue, the game servers for the following titles will be temporarily unavailable on all platforms," the RPG studio tweeted earlier today, before naming Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3.

While the server shutdown won't last forever, FromSoftware hasn't told series fans when exactly they can expect online play to be restored. That presumably means PvP invasions, summon signs and in-game messages that try to troll you off a cliff are unavailable for the time being.

"We will provide updates once we have information regarding the server restoration time. We apologize for the inconvenience," the studio added. I hope you've stocked up on Estus Flasks, at least.

Of course, this isn't the first time the Dark Souls trilogy has had to contend with server problems. In 2022, Bandai Namco took servers for all three Dark Souls games offline due to a security vulnerability affecting Dark Souls 3. The threequel went dark once again a few months later.

FromSoftware's next game The Duskbloods - the one with the jetpacks and vampires and a cute bird thing - hasn't been any luckier, either. The multiplayer-focused game's first network test had to be taken offline early due to similarly vague "server issues". More recently, FromSoftware delayed its Switch 2 exclusive into next year.

"While development of The Duskbloods is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027," the developer tweeted this week. "We apologise to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support."

#3790. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Link’s Tunic Looks Like That Because He Made It Himself

The Legend of ZeldaThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

When the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was first revealed, one of the most common gut reactions I saw across the internet was in response to the game’s overall visual style. And everyone seemed to focus on one thing in particular: Link’s clothes.

Basically, Link’s clothes feature a ridiculous amount of detail. They appear to be hand-woven out of some sort of fiber, and you can see every stitch. There’s a fringe around the bottom, and larger stitches where the sleeves attach and where his hat comes together. Over his tunic, he’s wearing some sort of leather armor with swirling leaf designs. Adult Link’s boots have similar etchings. It all looks…not hyperrealistic or anything, but it certainly has an over-the-top amount of intricacy that the Nintendo 64 Link never could have dreamed of.

There was debate, though, as to whether this was good or not. Some people compared it to the look of Unreal Engine fan games, which have been oft-mocked for missing the simplistic charm of typical Nintendo games. A lot of people felt that Link stood out from his surroundings, especially when he stood next to other NPCs with less detail, such as some folks in Castle Town. But others really liked the tunic and its details, and noted how well it spoke to Link’s origins as a child of the forest.

Well according to the game’s developers, that history is exactly what they were tapping into with the tunic’s intricate look. In an Ask the Developer interview today, art director Aya Shida and producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained how the tunic (and the rest of the art style) came to be. Shida begins by saying the team didn’t take changing the designs lightly, and began by making sketches of the characters to place side-by-side with the old designs, as well as a 3D model of the Great Deku Tree. “We wanted characters like these to blend naturally into a world like this.”

The sketches made by the team don’t look more realistic than the old designs. But the original designs did have significant limits placed upon them by the Nintendo 64’s technology, as Fujibayashi explains:

Back when games were being developed for Nintendo 64, there were limits to what could be expressed in-game. With those limitations in mind, the developers chose to exaggerate the charactersâ movements and defining features so that their distinctive qualities would come through. But if we recreated all of that precisely with today’s technology, it might look a little creepy. (Laughs) I imagine it was quite a challenge to strike the right balance while still preserving each character’s individuality.

Fujibayashi ends by noting that in the new game, there was a lot of attention given to clothing textures now that those limitations have been removed. As an example, Shida offers Young Link’s outfit.

If the fabric looked too neat, as though it had been machine-woven, it wouldn’t look like something the children living in the forest had made themselves. It just wouldn’t feel believable.

So we started by asking what kind of fabric those children might actually weave and wear. We looked at materials in museums and even experimented with making our own fabric from thread to get a better sense of what it should be like. For this game, the hardware allowed us to depict that level of detail, but that also meant we needed to do our research until we had a clear idea of what we wanted to create. As a design team, we often talked about imagining the story behind every object in the game as we created it.

So essentially, while Link’s smooth tunic was fine for the Nintendo 64’s capabilities, on the souped-up Switch 2, a smooth tunic might have looked ridiculous on him and the other Kokiri given what we know about their lore. So instead, the team did a bunch of (frankly very cool) research to work out what sort of clothing would make sense for him and his brethren, clothing which would naturally be quite different from what everyone outside the forest was wearing.

The rest of the interview is pretty cool and worth reading, though if you’re just looking for highlights, you can read real quick about Eiji Aonuma adding, and then removing, more fast travel points to the game. A second part to the interview will be out tomorrow, and the remake of Ocarina of Time is out later this week, on November 5.

#3789. Dave Bautista shows off Kratos physique after gaining 20 pounds of muscle for God of War TV series

From WWE to Guardian of the Galaxy to God of War, Dave Bautista is really flexing, both literally and figuratively.

It’s been just over two months since Dave Bautista was confirmed as the new Kratos in the Amazon Prime Video God of War series, replacing injured actor Ryan Hurst, but the man formerly known as WWE’s “The Animal” proudly displayed his god-like physique on Instagram yesterday.

Bautista says he’s now at 250 pounds, which is still quite a bit lighter than what he used to wrestle at in the WWE, when he routinely took to the ring at around 290. But after retiring from in-ring competition and focusing on acting, he’s since lost a lot of that weight and began putting it back on this summer.

Bautista was announced as Hurst’s replacement on Aug. 20, just a few months after the latter tore his pectoral muscle while filming and forcing Prime Video to scramble. Bautista was waiting in the wings, and he since got to work in the gym to be ready to get into the white and red paint and play father to a demigod.

It’s been fun to watch Bautista’s career, coming from his wrestling beginnings, to then taking on the role of Drax the Destroyer in the Marvel Cinematic Universe for several years of fun and iconic moments, and moving on to all sorts of varied acting roles since. This may be his biggest challenge yet, however, as he’s now 57 years old and this is quite a physically demanding role, as evidenced by Hurst’s on-set injury that helped land him the job.

Outside of Bautista, the God of War show’s cast is stacked, boasting a pantheon of Norse mythology along with talented actors: Callum Vinson as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, Ed Skrein as Baldur, Max Parker as Heimdall, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor, Teresa Palmer as Sif, Alastair Duncan as Mimir, Jeff Gulka as Sindri, Danny Woodburn as Brok, and more.

Dave Bautista reveals he has gained 20 more pounds of muscle for playing Kratos in ‘GOD OF WAR’.He has now reached 250 pounds. pic.twitter.com/fUOr0P7EAB

There’s currently no premiere date set for God of War on Prime Video, but it’s likely at least a year away, as Bautista now begins shooting and reshooting scenes that already took place early this summer with Hurst.

The Punished, coming soon to the outstanding deckbuilder, draw their power from self-flagellation.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Their aesthetic? Chains, whips; spiked. Their mood? Afflicted, condemned, ritualistic. Their angels? Dark. Their maiden? Iron.

Friendship ended with dwarven gearsmiths; my new favorite clan in Monster Train 2 is the tortured edgelords.

The final faction being added to Monster Train 2, The Punished, arrive November 10 as a paid DLC. Their theme is self-damage, with new keywords and spells that, primarily, reward power in exchange for hurting yourself. Your pain? Enemies' bane.

Though existing MT2 clans like the Melting Remnant revolve around forms of sacrifice, The Punished are absolutely thirsty for it. They bring new keywords like Chained (enemy units take half the damage that your units take) that make damage an active solution to enemy waves. The self-flagellation angle likewise brings new purpose to some existing spells and equipment, and jives great with partner clans that provide protection from pain (Lazarus League) or more ways to inflict it (Pyreborne).

Damaging my own guys sounds like a risk-reward tactic that requires sophisticated play. In my first run as The Punished, I anticipated having to do brain-wracking calculus about how much damage to absorb. But instead, I've found the new clan to be one of the most powerful and, at least with one of their champions, easy to play.

A lot of that is down to the utility of their new gimmick, a big purple gem called the Monolith. Here's a breakdown of what makes it special:

"Level up the Monolith by sacrificing cards to earn Devotion, which grants Zeal, which buffs attack and HP for all units" kind of sounds like a line from a ProZD deckbuilder parody video (I will take any opportunity to reference the legendary Dairy Cow combo), but it's really not complicated. Click the purple crystal, make cards go away, permascale a little bit.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Though it can change the calculus for a few units, Zeal isn't that game-breaking on its own: usually you're just increasing the ceiling of a unit's HP to set up cards like Zealot's Halo, an equipment that gives +1 attack for every 1 HP you're missing.

More potent is The Punished's starter champion, Archus, an S-tier champ that amps damage based on lost HP, but has the versatility to debuff enemy damage as well. All of his build paths grant him Flight. His best variant deploys a "Darkshard" into the lane he flies into, a 0-attack artifact that does one of the following, on your choice:

Bloodshed is really, really powerful with the right unit pairings and a cheap spell or two that hurts yourself. What's wild is that Archus can deploy a Darkshard in every lane, with a cooldown of 2 on his flight ability. I might anticipate a nerf on that. Scaling your whole floor from received hits (including self-targeted spells!) is a wonderful way to accelerate sweepers or backline bruisers. Archus good.

Zariel, the other champ, is more advanced. The first angel cast out of heaven, "Zariel has been imprisoned for so long that her original crime has been forgotten to time." Sick. Although, you'd think that that would enable some kind of clemency?

Since her arms and wings are bound in chains, Zariel has no base attack. What she does have are three diverse paths that all play off sponging up as much damage as possible:

I asked Shiny Shoe CEO Mark Cooke what combos the studio has found useful with Zariel. "A lot of Hellhorned cards like Branding Rite, Dark Deal, and Inferno work really well with Zariel's Pain and Chain paths. Pox is a great spell for consistent friendly damage, because it applies Decay 10 to all units," says Cooke. "Zariel's Pain Maiden path especially synergizes well with The Condemned, because the unit has Tenacious, it won't die to any friendly damage and it even amplifies the damage it takes and redirects it to an enemy, so it's great for pinging and stacking Pain while still killing enemies."

On my second run with Zariel, in the final rounds of a battle, I was dealing 1000 damage from her Paintouch ability, and I was doing it each turn because the ability has a cooldown of 1. On a couple other attempts, I couldn't create damage outputting units to pair with her quickly enough, and my run collapsed.

The superstar of the roster might be Penitent Sentinel, an uncommon tank that becomes MT2's most durable frontliner.

This is one of the few weaknesses of The Punished—although several units have good base attack, instantaneous damage can be hard to acquire. Reaper of Suffering, The Punished's only sweeper, starts with a generous 60 attack (as much as Demon Fiend, a 4-cost Hellhorned unit), but it also starts Suppressed (meaning she cannot attack), needing a cooldown of 4 to expire before she emerges from that state. Taking damage decreases that cooldown, and incredibly, she heals to full HP when she emerges from Supressed and gains flight when you cross that threshold.

This isn't the only star unit on The Punished. Forsaken Berserker gains one multistrike for every two Monolith levels. Scarred Justicar, an uncommon, ended up being my damage solution on several runs. He simply gains +15 attack when hit by a friendly spell or ability, and considering one of the starter cards deals a gentle 2 damage, you can gain perhaps +30 or +45 attack in a round between spells and other effects. Slap a stack of multistrike and the new 3-cost equipment Sineater on him (Deal 8 damage to self, attack immediately, cooldown 2), and you have a high damage solution that just takes a little time to set up.

The superstar of the roster, though, might be Penitent Sentinel, an uncommon tank that becomes MT2's most durable frontliner if you're able to draft it early. This stoic statue unit cannot be healed, but it gains +1 HP on revenge, astoundingly rare health permascaling that is set-and-forget simple. I found myself taking the "enemies gain multistrike" trial just to welcome more attacks against Penitent Sentinel. In some runs I was ending with nearly 300 HP, linked to a Titanite upgrade that effectively doubled that. Wild.

After 12 wins with The Punished, I love that they have several viable units to pick from, and how much they synergize with a variety of clans. I kept finding new ways of winning with Zariel, and my strangest victory was with this configuration:

I had no plan and was mostly freestyling through this, my upgrade selections weren't particularly strong. I was surprised to beat Savagery, let alone the Titans.

After 500 hours in Monster Train 2, it's refreshing to beat the game in an unexpected way. I truly thought this run was doomed because I had little traditional damage, no sweep, no tank, and no decapitating spells.

The Punished's masochistic theme works. And Shiny Shoe's treatment of these tortured angels is nice (their Carolina Panthers-blue skin helps them stand out, even among the pale blue Melting Remnant), though their stoic reverence doesn't leave a lot of room for quirk.

I would've loved to have seen a silly torture sicko among the roster, but I'll settle for Lasher, the first backline unit that hits any friendly units positioned in front of him for 1 damage (I don't recommend relying on Damage Shield when he's on the floor). Just think of it as giving your guys a helpful, spiked-chain pat on the back.

It's appropriate for the final update to a game I like a lot to hurt a little. But Shiny Shoe CEO Mark Cooke did indicate that the studio may not be done with the franchise. "At this time The Punished is the last DLC planned for MT2," Cooke told me. "However, we love the world of Monster Train, and hope to work on more Monster Train games in the future!"

#3787. Blizzard hints at console ports for World of Warcraft: Forever - "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want"

After more than two decades dominating the PC MMO battlefield, it sounds like Blizzard Entertainment's taking the idea of a World of Warcraft console port more seriously than ever.

World of Warcraft: Forever's beta seems to have been immensely popular with fans of the series. It's a brand new third version of the iconic multiplayer game that sits alongside WoW's Classic and Retail portions, and it's recaptured many a lapsed Warcraft sicko with tons of good changes, big and small - one of which is controller support for the first time ever.

Speaking to GamesRadar about the decision to keep World of Warcraft: Forever exclusive to PC players, despite now supporting gamepads, vice president and executive producer Holly Longdale hinted that the fantasy game might just make its way to even more devices and players over time.

"What you just described is really what we're after," she told the outlet. "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want. But the first leg of that journey is getting gamepads working really well with World of Warcraft, and we thought Forever was the perfect place to start."

Longdale reckons all gaming platforms might become "more ubiquitous" in the future, as well. She specifically named the Xbox Project Helix, which is said to be a PC-console hybrid device of some kind. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed the next-gen console can even play your PC games earlier in the year.

"Honestly, we just want to be able to play it anywhere. We've seen people getting it working on the ROG Ally X," Longdale added. "I think just doing some of the work we're doing on gamepad is going to give players a lot of flexibility that I think goes beyond consoles."

World of Warcraft: Forever properly launches on the 4th of November.

Despite struggles in the rest of the Xbox division, Forever's beta was supposedly the "largest" in series history. Elsewhere, Longdale acknowledged that some of the developer's decisions won't make everybody equally happy: "I think the lesson we learned the most over time is 'You don't listen to the loudest people in the room.'"

Celebrities brought their A-game this Halloween. From Megan Fox going full Twilight as a gothic vampire to Carmen Electra dressing as Catwoman, A-listers truly sought to lean on creativity and individuality when devising their looks for the holiday. As for Jennifer Lopez, she decided to go for a topless look to channel her Monster-In-Law co-star, Jane Fonda, while dressing as the powerful Barbarella.

Jennifer Lopez has proved time and again this year what a fashionista she is. Most recently, she looked dreamy and romantic at Paris Fashion Week wearing a sheer dress and brought fall vibes in a fur coat and sheer, luxe black dress. For Halloween, you couldn’t expect anything less, as her Barberella look was not only fierce but also served as a fitting tribute to one of Jane Fonda's most distinct movie roles. Check it out in the Instagram post below:

For those who don’t know, Barbarella is a campy cult classic that sees Fonda portraying a futuristic female astronaut who encounters strange planets while trying to locate Dr. Durand-Durand. One of the Roger Vadim-directed sci-fi flick’s most memorable qualities is the array of outlandish futuristic costumes that Fonda wears. With that in mind, Lopez couldn’t have picked a better movie to channel for her Halloween costume this year.

The Maid in Manhattan actress is showing the right to bear arms while wearing Barbarella’s mesh silver-laced dress with metallic boots. I’m also loving the white bodysuit with the black vertical stripes running down. The ‘60s blonde wig she’s wearing as the aforementioned character is such a nice nod to the decade and fictional space heroines in general.

And Lopez can’t celebrate the cult classic’s sexual liberation theme without taking a topless photo of herself, which sees her posing with blind angel Pylar. All in all, JLo looks like she’s having a lot of fun honoring her former co-star’s psychedelic movie.

With how on-point Jennifer Lopez looks as Barbarella, you’d think she was auditioning for the remake of the 1968 film. I mean, she’s wearing each outfit with such pizzazz and poise. However, Sydney Sweeney is set to “save the universe” as the film's lead. The actress seems like a great fit, and I'm confident she'll do a great job embodying the iconic space adventurer.

Per what's known about the remake, Edgar Wright has been in talks to direct, while Kingsman's Jane Goldman and Honey Ross have also been approached to write the screenplay. While the upcoming science-fiction movie is still in its development stages, it’s great that the “On the Floor” singer is already bringing the movie back into the general public's consciousness.

When it comes to the long line of costumes Jennifer Lopez has worn for Halloween over the years, these Barbarella looks may be amongst my favorites. If anything, now I'd like to know how Jane Fonda feels about her former co-star paying tribute to her and her character. In the meantime, anyone who's curious and wants to check out Barbarella can do so by watching the movie for free on Pluto TV.

#3785. All Vault locations in Fortnite Treasure Hunters and how to get keys

Although treasures are a common sight while exploring the new One Piece-themed areas in Fortnite Treasure Hunters, vaults are still the best places to find those sought-after Pirate Shop Activation tokens and Legendary Sprites.

But don’t worry, you won’t need a master navigator or a Devil Fruit to find any of them. Here are all vault locations in Fortnite Treasure Hunters and how to get the keys needed to open them.

You can find a total of nine vaults scattered across the new Fortnite Treasure Hunters map, with most of its main regions housing one. The exceptions? Arlong Park, The Chest, and Plunder Port. In all areas but The $.$ Rocky, the vaults will be hidden behind a breakable sheet wall and located by a red flag.

The vaults can be opened by using universal Vault Keys and will house both a series of rare Treasure Chests and a guaranteed Sprite Chest. So prioritize them when looking to complete all steps in the Treasure Hunt Quest.

Among the locations above, reaching the Loot Laggon vault will require entering its secret area within the waterfall, while the one at Loguetown can only be found by heading to the city’s underground aqueduct.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Fortnite players can get Vault Keys as a rare loot by opening chests across the island or by eliminating players carrying them. When looking for one, we recommend focusing your search on either Busy Bay or Rubber Resort via their high number of guaranteed chest spawns per drop.

Certain sprites can also drop keys after leveling up, as well as boost your chances of finding them from regular chests. To learn more, check out all Sprites and abilities in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.

While in possession of a key, the locations of the closest locked vaults will be marked on your map. As many will also be heading towards them, I recommend prioritizing the vault at Loot Laggon. After all, its natural camouflage might make most players pass it by and lower the chances that you might have to fight for the loot after unlocking it.

Unlike the first season, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners IIâs story takes place after the events of Cyberpunk 2077. As such, fans have been looking throughout the anime for any sign of characters from CD Projekt Redâs RPG, including V, the customizable protagonist the player inhabits. However, since the show takes place post-2077, Vâs appearance would open up a whole messy box of questions about the showâs continuity and whether the broader Cyberpunk franchise now has a âcanonâ ending from the choice-driven game it will adhere to in stories set after Vâs adventures. In fact, those questions have already been raised, and according to showrunner Bartosz Sztybor, thereâs no intention of canonizing or invalidating any of the gameâs potential endings.

In an interview with IGN, Sztybor talked about what some fans believe to have been a V cameo in the new Edgerunners season, specifically of the âdefaultâ female V with a red undercut seen in the gameâs promotional artwork. The personâs face appears in an Arasaka database alongside other cyberware-compatible individuals (including Edgerunners season one protagonist David Martinez), and though the show doesnât make a big to-do about this person specifically, some fans are taking this as a sign that V is alive and in Night City in a post-2077 timeline. However, Sztybor says that any such read of the show is just fan speculation.

Yeah I ainât crazy thatâs deadass V https://t.co/bT6OmOWXDw pic.twitter.com/3XC5KtlrDa

— ð ð¼ð¿ð¶ ðsÌ¸sÌ¸ê³ð ð¯ð² ð½ (@_morijinn) October 20, 2026

âWe don’t want to set a canon ending,âÂ  he says. âSo there were a lot of conversations again with the lore team to see what we can do to somehow satisfy all the endings, and what will be the state of the world after the game. That’s why the scene that you asked about, we don’t want to be straightforward, but we are giving some suggestions that will probably reveal the state of the world in more comic books and other stuff. So there are discussions. There are discussions, but we are not setting one kind of ending.â

If held up to some scrutiny, the supposed V cameo is questionable. As some fans point out, the characterâs hairstyle isnât exactly the same as that of the âdefaultâ female V, and her cyberware isnât identical to that seen in 2077âs promo art, so even if the show were to be âcanonizingâ a specific version of V, this person doesnât look quite like the one you see on the gameâs box art. But ultimately, the show goes out of its way to not directly address Vâs fate, which can go in several directions depending on the playerâs choices.Â

âWhen we were creating Edgerunners [season one] and multiple comic books and board games, the canon was before the game, so we knew the state of the world.â he says. âAnd for the things post-game, it’s not that there are super-detailed canon things, but one important canon information is that Arasaka is weakened and that’s it. And it gives us a lot of opportunities to show the city in a different way.

But again, it’s not detailed. So it doesn’t make any of the endings canon. But the things that happened in the game could lead to that, whatever your choice was.â

I appreciate when creators for choice-driven franchises have this mindset, even if it means that future Cyberpunk projects canât incorporate characters who have multiple fates depending on the choices you make in 2077. Notably, Rogue, the owner of the Afterlife nightclub, makes a brief appearance in the first Edgerunners season, but is never seen in the second season, likely because she can die in one of the gameâs endings. It takes characters who exist in quantum states off the board, but it better allows all fans to enjoy a work without feeling like their choices are being portrayed as incorrect or invalid.

#3783. GOTY hopeful Mina the Hollower bought the studio financial stability "for now," while the Shovel Knight devs work on a new 3D game

Yacht Club Games has confirmed that most of its developers are now working on a brand new 3D game (potentially Shovel Knight 3D), after the critically-acclaimed Mina the Hollower did well enough for the team to continue.

Before launching its old-school adventure game earlier this year, Yacht Club described Mina the Hollower as a "make-or-break" moment for the beloved indie studio. A global pandemic and a failed experiment to turn Yacht Club into a multi-project studio had left the developer on thin ice, it seems.

But Mina the Hollower sold well enough to buy the studio more time, according to a new Reddit AMA full of interesting tidbits. Asked if Mina was able to secure financial stability for the company, Sean Velasco simply said "yes… for now!" Mina managed to sell over 500,000 copies in its first two weeks, so it's well on its way to the one million copies the devs were once hoping for.

For the foreseeable future, the devs aren't ready to talk about the kinds of DLC and spin-offs and follow-ups that dear old Shovel Knight enjoyed for many years, but they're not abandoning their newest baby either. "We're working on more post-release features," the devs wrote, which includes "expanded randomizer options, enemy and boss randomization, more modifiers, speedrunner features" and more ways "to do even more in Mina."

Another fan also asked the folks at Yacht Club about their unannounced 3D Shovel Knight game - Velasco previously told Bloomberg that the game was halfway done before the entire studio put all hands on deck for Mina, and pivoted back into a one-game outfit. Alec Faulkner stopped short of confirming Shovel Knight 3D, but said "most of us are currently working on a 3D game, yes!" Alright then, Alec, keep your secrets. "Not sayin more! Other than that it’s gonna be soooooooo awesome."

Co-founder Nick Wozniac went further into the state of the developer, and why splitting the team in half was probably a mistake. Here's what he had to say on the matter: "Sales are the things that keep the company afloat so it's not born from greed (mostly) that we say we'd love to see more sales, it's all about continuing to work together and make great games and reaping the rewards along the way. We are doing ok and learned a lot this cycle. I think we learned mostly that keeping the team tight and focused is what helped Mina land. Splitting the team up to work on two games was something we could have corrected a long time ago but I'm glad to be where we are now. Just gotta pocket those lessons and use them to drive you forward."

Eurogamer's five-star Mina the Hollower review called it an "adventure that takes inspiration from the greats."

Preorders are opening up for physical editions of Nightdive's Thief Remaster, and at the high end, the studio is offering an homage to Thief's iconic original PC big box packaging in that shape we all know and love, the trapezoid. The only problem? Nightdive and partner Clear River Games are only offering it for Switch/Switch 2 and PS5.

It doesn't really, at least not as much as war and death and politics or whatever. But Thief's original '90s big box edition came in a jaunty little trapezoidal box unlike anything else on the market. It remains a visually striking, highly sought-after collector's item. It's fun, it's memorable, and it's a piece of PC gaming history. I've had to settle for my version of Thief Gold that came in a plain Jane regular box as a reissue.

It's not super surprising that Night Dive and Clear River eschewed a PC version of this physical release⁠—that's fairly common these days, even in boutique indie special editions. I had a similar "we're so back, it's so over" reaction when I saw that indie RPG heater Dread Delusion's limited physical edition had skipped PC.

But the hurt feels new all over again when it's a PC gaming icon like Thief, and a PC gaming phenomenon like the big box. I would have dropped a fat hundo on a physical PC version of Thief Remastered in a heartbeat⁠—it's why I live in an apartment and not a house.

And studios still do come out with physical editions of their PC games: My Baldur's Gate 3 big box has pride of place in my office. All told, it's just a slight bummer and frustration trying to drag down one of my most anticipated games. I'm still going to play the hell out of it when it comes out on December 3, though.

I'm rooting for GOG's proposal to bring back the big box. The company seems to be considering a boutique service where you can purchase physical versions of the games in your library, which sounds pretty rad to me.

#3781. A former volunteer is threatening legal action against fan-made game project Skyblivion

A former volunteer is threatening legal action against Skyblivion, the long-running fan remake of Oblivion built in Skyrim's engine, over code they contributed to the project.

The unofficial project, which remakes 2006's The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion, is being made by volunteers from the TES Renewal Project, the modding group that also works on Morrowind remake Skywind.

Bethesda has allowed the project to continue on condition that it replaces all of the original game's assets, and the team continued working on it after Bethesda released its own Oblivion Remastered in April 2025.

In a statement posted to Twitter/X on 30th October, the Skyblivion team said that after the volunteer left, the two sides disagreed over the "continued use and maintenance" of their work.

A former volunteer is attempting to sue Skyblivion and we need your help pic.twitter.com/3Ee5eQTELG

The main issue was the team's decompilation of parts of that code, which it said was needed "to maintain functionality and fix issues" after its access to the original source code repository was revoked.

According to the team, the volunteer then "escalated to sending legal threats", including demands for the real names and home addresses of its volunteer team leads. The team said this was "something we couldn't accept and think is disproportionate".

The team said it has consulted legal counsel and is "completely confident in our right to maintain the code they submitted". Even so, it said it removed the code "to protect our volunteers from undue stress and ensure a clean break", rebuilding that system from scratch.

Despite this, it says the threats have continued. Its post says the former volunteer is "attempting to sue", but it's not clear whether a lawsuit has actually been filed. The volunteer has not been named.

"Please don't make this a witch-hunt," the team told fans, adding that it wishes the former volunteer "the very best" and hopes to "get this resolved as soon as possible and get on with our planned release of Skyblivion".

Last December, the team delayed Skyblivion from 2025 into 2026.

Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything has been stirring up buzz and earning its fair share of money. However, one honor that had been alluding it was the No. 1 spot at the box office. Well, that's no longer the case, as the doc finally became the top movie in the United States this weekend. And regardless of whether that win can be attributed to people showing up because of all the Oscar buzz, or the scene that literally shows everything, it's also resulted in the documentary obtaining a very rare honor.

It should be mentioned that Fielder's film just barely won the top spot, as Warner Bros. and DC Studios' Clayface just missed winning Halloween weekend after its strong start by a little less than $200,000. Wildwood, which some are calling one of the best and scariest movies of the year, remains in third place this week, while steamy fantasy flick Wicker climbed another spot too. Check out the full breakdown below:

6. BTS World Tour ‘Arirang’ in Buenos Aires and São Paulo Live Viewing

9. The Only Living Pickpocket In New York

The No. 1 spot aside, this is a truly auspicious moment for You Can See Everything, because in a rare turn of events, it's now the fourth documentary ever to win a weekend box office. With that, it now joins Fahrenheit 9/11, Michael Jackson's This Is It and Taylor Swift: The Official Release Of A Showgirl. That's a lineup even more wtf than some of the moments in the film. Nevertheless, this is quite the distinction for Fielder and co.

I Wondered Why Nathan Fielder Was Picked For You Can See Everything. His Answer Confused Me

One way YCSE differentiates itself from this lineup, however, is by having a different path to this milestone. All three of the other movies managed to win the box office in their opening weekends. You Can See Everything opened at No. 2 at the box office weeks ago and held that spot last week before finally grabbing the top spot this week.

Whether Fielder's film will hold that spot again next week remains to be seen. Clayface is still sticking around, and it had about 200 more theaters screening the body horror thriller this weekend. That comic book film is already proving to be a solid win for DC, as it has grossed roughly $83 million worldwide against a reported budget between $30 and $44 million.

Plus, a new month means a new slate of films arriving on the 2026 movie schedule. The Cat in the Hat and Godzilla Minus Zero are among the titles arriving in a week's time, and there's always the chance that they could shake things up at the B.O. next week.

All this to say, I expect You Can See Everything to stick around the Top 10 for at least a few more weeks based on how it's trending. I'm very curious as to just how much longer it'll continue to haul in millions, as I don't know if anyone saw this run coming. I'm just hoping to hear that this means Nathan Fielder is going to get more documentaries in theaters, which I would absolutely love to see.

#3779. Nearly 50 percent of all of last month’s Steam releases admit to containing AI slop

It seems like AI-generated content in video games isn’t going anywhere any time soon. In fact, it’s only getting worse.

A Redditor named ploz dug deep into the stats to find that 49.9 percent of all new games released in October 2026 disclosed that they were made with AI-generated content, which is a big increase from 26.4 percent one year ago. The scary part? The chart below begins in January 2024 (when Steam added AI disclosure options), when it was just 1.7 percent.

But the details don’t end there, as ploz revealed that 40.1 percent of all games released in 2026 so far use the AI-generated content tag. And in actuality, the number is likely way higher as there are sure to be devs that don’t disclose their AI usage in the listings, plus the AI disclosure only counts content you see or hear, and not anything used in coding.

The Redditor said it’s “mostly small games” that use the AI tag, saying that “47 percent of games with fewer than 10 reviews disclose AI, compared to 14 percent of games with 1,000+ reviews.” That’s not all that surprising, considering a lot of the AI-centric titles are made by smaller devs or those trying to quickly make a few bucks, but the reality is likely much different.

It feels like using AI to code is certainly not going anywhere, and I can’t really imagine how many devs are utilizing this to make their games, although I’d venture a guess to say it’s more than we even realize or could think of, considering it doesn’t need to be disclosed. Where it feels especially egregious is when it can be seen or heard or felt through things like dialogue, music, or in-game imagery.

For now, though, Steam does not offer a way to filter out games with AI-generated content from the store entirely, and as evidenced by this most recent Steam Next Fest, many players are annoyed with how outwardly obvious some of the games are becoming with their “AI slop.” Valve recently said it was “aware” of the complaints, but there’s no real timetable for a solution either.

#3777. Silent Hill: Townfall adds new Hard difficulty in latest update

Silent Hill: Townfall has added a new Hard difficulty mode and rebalanced every existing setting to make room for it.

The update, patch 1.6.0, went live on PS5, Steam, and the Epic Games Store earlier this week, according to patch notes published by Konami. Konami said the rebalance is designed to create "a smoother difficulty curve for players to choose from".

As part of that rebalance, resources have been adjusted in some sections of the game, and enemies' hearing now gets sharper as the difficulty level goes up. Your position is now visible on the map in whichever mode you pick, while the reduction to the main enemy's attack severity now applies only in Story Mode.

Anyone who picks Nightmare for their first playthrough will now see a warning screen. The difficulty selection menu also gives a clearer summary of how the options differ.

SILENT HILL: TownfallNotice: Game Update (Patch 1.6.0)An update tuning gameplay and addressing some in-game issues is now available.Please check that the version number in the lower right corner of the main menu is displayed as v1.6.155963.*The PlayStation®5 version is…

The update also improves the valve status lighting for colourblind players, adds more hints and tutorials, and tweaks the wording of some puzzle hints and items. The options menu has been reorganised into clearer categories, and the controls remapping option has been renamed to make it clear that keyboard and mouse commands can be remapped there too, not just controllers.

PC players also get a new DLSS Ray Reconstruction option, alongside the usual general improvements and bug fixes.

To check you're on the latest version, look for v1.6.155963 in the lower right corner of the main menu on PC, or v1.6.156035 on PS5.

Developed by Screen Burn and published by Konami, Silent Hill: Townfall launched on PS5 and PC on 24th September. Matt said Townfall showed Silent Hill's "stellar revival continues as new developer Screen Burn melds stealth, meticulous world design, and a dash of social realism for a different sort of survival horror", and awarded it four out of five stars in Eurogamer's Silent Hill: Townfall review.

I've been a big fan of comedian Grace Reiter since I first saw her on TikTok, and her recent addition to the Saturday Night Live cast has only elevated her star power. I was excited to see she's a part of streaming comedy doing well, as those with a Netflix subscription are finding out about Minimum Wage.

The series follows the young employees of "The Slice Club," a pizza franchise operating across the United States. It all kicks off when Randall Park's Terry Sylvester shows up for an impromptu visit as the company's CEO. I was psyched to see Park in the series and eager to see how the show developed, so I was disappointed when the series largely went on without acknowledging him.

I hadn't gotten enough of Randall Park on the 2026 TV schedule, and I don't have enough of him on Minimum Wage. The pilot sets the stage perfectly with his introduction, and even ends with him moving into the basement of the pizza shop, determined to turn around the lowest-performing store's numbers.

He then proceeds to appear in very little of the series from that point onward. It's baffling considering he is such a television staple, and it almost gives the impression that he was shoehorned into the series at the late stages in order to give Minimum Wage a bit more star power. He never really has as much screen time as he does in the first episode, and most scenes after are only a couple of minutes long.

We have no idea if future seasons of Minimum Wage are part of Netflix's upcoming schedule. If it does return, however, I would humbly request that Randall Park's Terry Sylvester have a larger role in the show than he did in Season 1.

The One Thing Matthew Perry's Sister Loves About The Netflix Documentary Telling Her Brother's Story

To me, the fun in this show is a bunch of teens awkwardly dealing with a middle-aged man experiencing a midlife crisis. While I did enjoy the workplace antics and some of the downsides of serving a room full of theater kids, I feel like the well for content on that can only go so deep.

I do question if Grace Reiter's Saturday Night Live schedule will allow her to continue to commit time to Minimum Wage if it returns for another season. It does seem like more SNL stars than ever are popping up in projects while also doing the show, rather than striking off on their own after a couple of years. I think it has potential, provided they can tweak the series a bit to include more of Randall Park.

Watch Minimum Wage on Netflix right now, as well as all of the other great shows on the platform! I'm still obsessed with The Boroughs despite it being cancelled, and come to think of it, maybe it would've benefitted from having Randall Park involved as well.

#3775. Final Fantasy 14 reveals Evercold’s second new job and February release date, with pre-orders opening next week

Plus Square Enix confirms Final Fantasy 14 has passed 35m registered accounts.

Final Fantasy 14's next expansion, Evercold, will launch on 23rd February 2027, and its second new job is zephyr, a physical ranged DPS that fights with a crossbow and a bird.

Producer and director Naoki Yoshida revealed the job during the opening keynote of the Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo. Zephyr pairs crossbow shots with support from an avian familiar called Nephele, and joins Bastion, the greatshield-wielding tank revealed as Evercold's first new job at Fan Festival Berlin earlier this year.

Pre-orders for Evercold and the previously announced Collector's Box open on Wednesday 4th November at 9am GMT. Anyone who pre-orders gets early access, plus a Wind-Up Köttr minion and Halone's Earring, which boosts EXP from defeating enemies by 30 percent. The in-game items are delivered as soon as you pre-order, so you can use the earring to level jobs before Evercold arrives.

The Collector's Box is physical goods only. It doesn't include the game, in-game items or pre-order bonuses. Inside you'll find an art box featuring an Evercold illustration by Yoshitaka Amano, a figure of the Warrior of Light as a reaper, an Ethos metal keychain, a Köttr mini plush, and a Tapestry of the Fourth.

The Square Enix Store is also selling a limited Collector's Bundle that pairs the box with a code for the Digital Collector's Edition on Windows or Mac. Players on PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, and Steam can buy the box on its own and pre-order the Digital Collector's Edition separately. The digital edition adds a Valhallar Odin mount, an Entreat Crystal emote, and a Crystal Skyltborg weapon for Bastion.

Square Enix also used the keynote to reveal a new Fierce raid difficulty, sitting between Normal and Savage; a new trailer for the Evangelion: Ghosts of Desire alliance raid crossover, plus tougher eight-player battles built around some of its bosses; and new Tetsuya Nomura artwork for Beyond the Lifestream, a raid series crossover with the Final Fantasy 7 Remake series.

We can also expect Evolved Combat Mode, which Square Enix says highlights each job's unique identity; Seasons, a new system that changes how item rewards are earned; and expanded character creation with new Character Action Skins. Expanded housing features, PvP updates, and a revamped companion chocobo system will follow from patch 8.1.

Final Fantasy 14 has passed 35 million registered accounts.

You can watch the full keynote on Twitch, and there's more on the official Evercold site.

Final Fantasy 14 is now available on Switch 2. The port was announced at the end of June.
